{{Short description|American geneticist (1934–2000)}}
'''John David Axtell''' (February 5, 1934 – December 2, 2000) was an American geneticist, Lynn Distinguished Professor of Agronomy,<ref name="NAP">[http://www.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=10683&page=3 National Academies Press, V.82, JOHN DAVID AXTELL]</ref> member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="NAP"/> Axtell received the Alexander von Humboldt Award in 1975,<ref name="NAP"/> the Crop Science Research Award from the Crop Science Society of America in 1976,<ref name="NAP"/> and the International Award for Distinguished Service to Agriculture in 1984.<ref name="NAP"/> Axtell was widely noted for his research on [[sorghum]] (''[[Sorghum bicolor]]'' L.).<ref name="NAP"/><ref>[https://select.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=F10811FA3554137A93CBAB1782D85F478785F9&scp=1&sq=%22John%20D%20Axtell%22&st=cse ''The New York Times'':Research Finds Rich Sorghums To Bolster Diet of World's Poor; Research Finds Rich Sorghums to Aid the Poor, September 29, 1973],</ref> ''[[The New York Times]]'' and other sources reported that Axtell had been one of discoverers of high-[[lysine]] sorghum, and that the discovery was crucial to the fight against world hunger.<ref name="NAP"/>
<ref>[https://select.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=FB071EFC395F137B93C3A8178BD95F408785F9&scp=4&sq=%22John%20D%20Axtell%22&st=cse Search for Protein Crucial In Struggle Against Hunger; Studied Protein in Corn]</ref><ref>[http://www.sorghumgrowers.com/Magazine/Fall%202009%20SG%20web.pdf SORGHUM Grower Fall 2009.indd]{{dead link|date=April 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==  Career and life ==
Axtell was born in [[Minneapolis, Minnesota]], on February 5, 1934. He received his B.S. degree in agronomy and plant genetics in 1957 from the [[University of Minnesota]], M.S. degree in plant genetics in 1965, and Ph.D. degree in plant genetics in 1967, the last from [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]. Axtell spent his entire academic career 34 years at [[Purdue University]], starting in 1967 right after completing requirements for his Ph.D. degree. He became a full professor in 1975, and Lynn Distinguished Professor of Agronomy in 1982.
